issues.where: far left edge, mid-frame, frames 1544-1550 (rise cover)
issues.what: a bright, sharp-edged white cloud fragment appears at the left border and stays pinned there while the rest of the view moves, so the edge of a terrain layer comes into frame
issues.fix: overscan the terrain plate or layer so its border never comes into frame during the cover, or mask or feather the layer edge

issues.what: during the cover the globe render dissolves over the terrain view, which gives two limbs at once: an orange-brown rim sitting above a pale horizon, with a cold blue strip between them. It reads as two pictures cross-fading, not one move
issues.fix: match the terrain horizon curvature and atmosphere color to the globe limb before the blend, or drive both from one camera so the limbs line up through the cover

issues.what: the descent ground smears into directional streaks and stretched texels, with blocky upscaled cloud relief. It looks like a stretched texture, not motion blur over real relief
issues.fix: load higher-resolution surface detail as the camera closes in, and use true per-pixel motion blur in place of the stretched sampling

issues.what: same as in the dive: the terrain stretches and swims in long smeared streaks, the cloud relief turns into blocky stippling, and the low-detail texture shows as the camera pulls away
issues.fix: use the same fix as the dive: higher-resolution surface detail at close range and proper motion blur

issues.where: night side of the disc, lower right and right limb, all hold frames
issues.what: stars and pink Milky Way specks show through the planet's dark side, and a small bright point appears and disappears at different places near the right limb from frame to frame (1124, 1137, 1151, 1218, 1232, 1245). The globe reads as see-through, and the points pop
issues.fix: make the planet fully opaque over the starfield. If the bright point is meant to be a moon, give it a continuous orbit; if not, remove it

issues.what: the starfield and Milky Way fade to flat black during the dive and then return at full strength by 1317-1325, a visible exposure jump in the sky
issues.fix: keep the sky exposure continuous through the dive, or ramp it over many more frames

issues.what: a large change of framing between neighboring samples: the horizon, sun and sky are gone within about 7 frames and the view tilts down sharply. The pull-out lacks an eased start
issues.fix: ease the pitch-down and climb out over a longer ramp so the move starts with mass

issues.what: parallax is weak: the near clouds and the horizon drift almost together, and the sun and horizon stay fixed, so depth comes mostly from the clouds changing shape
issues.fix: add a slow forward or lateral camera move so the near cloud tops slide visibly against the horizon
